The clustered heatmap is the default way to look at an expression matrix: rows and columns reordered
by similarity, dendrograms on the margins, and sample metadata alongside. Here we build one in Python
with [canvasxpress](https://pypi.org/project/canvasxpress/) — clustering happens inside the render,
so you pass a plain matrix and get an interactive, reproducible figure.

## Install

```bash
pip install canvasxpress
```

## An expression matrix with sample metadata

Swap this simulated block for your own matrix (genes in rows, samples in columns) and a table of
per-sample annotations.

```{python}
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

rng   = np.random.default_rng(1)
ng, ns = 40, 30
genes = [f"Gene{i+1}" for i in range(ng)]
samps = [f"S{i+1}"    for i in range(ns)]
cond  = ["Tumor"] * (ns // 2) + ["Normal"] * (ns // 2)

m = rng.normal(0, 1, (ng, ns))
tumor = [i for i, c in enumerate(cond) if c == "Tumor"]
normal = [i for i, c in enumerate(cond) if c == "Normal"]
m[np.ix_(range(0, 20),  tumor)]  += 2      # first block up in Tumor
m[np.ix_(range(20, 40), normal)] += 2      # second block up in Normal

expr = pd.DataFrame(m.round(3), index=genes, columns=samps)
```

## Build the spec

The matrix goes in as `data`, and the sample annotation becomes an annotation track over the
columns. `samplesClustered` / `variablesClustered` turn on hierarchical clustering with dendrograms.

```{python}
from canvasxpress.canvas import CanvasXpress
from canvasxpress.render.jupyter import CXNoteBook

data = {
    "y": {"vars": genes, "smps": samps, "data": expr.values.tolist()},
    "x": {"Condition": cond},
}

config = {
    "graphType": "Heatmap",
    "samplesClustered": True, "variablesClustered": True,
    "colorSpectrum": ["navy", "white", "firebrick3"],
    "showSmpDendrogram": True, "showVarDendrogram": True,
    "title": "Clustered expression heatmap",
}

cx = CanvasXpress(render_to="heatmap", data=data, config=config, width=650, height=550)
CXNoteBook(cx).render()
```

Rows and columns are reordered by similarity, the dendrograms show the clustering, and the samples
separate cleanly by condition. Hover a cell for its gene, sample and value; the whole figure is one
portable spec you can store, validate and re-render from R or JavaScript.
